description:
1. **Question:** Why `MeetView` didn't use `MeetControls`, move the call controls into it, and review unused meet components.
2. **Finding:** `MeetControls` was a stale, voice-only, DaisyUI-styled bar with hard-disabled camera/screen-share buttons, so `MeetView` had reimplemented richer inline controls and never wired it back.
3. **Fix:** Rewrote `MeetControls.vue` as a small presentational controls bar (props in / emits out, no store coupling) and connected it in `MeetView.vue` with the `isInitiator` computed, re-activating the dead `onEndMeet()` method.
4. **Cleanup:** Deleted the orphaned `MeetSettingsPanel.vue`, an unused duplicate of the canonical `MeetSettingsModal.vue`.
5. **Outcome:** Components kept specialized and composite; the files had drifted since generation (a new `MicIndicator` component had been adopted), so changes were reviewed and reapplied with that convention.

Let me read these and related files.Now let me read the meet components directory and the API/session layer to understand the full integration.Let me read the meets API module, users store, and find where the meet view is opened.Let me check the router and the UI store to see how the meet view is opened and routed.Let me read the app config to confirm the meet app definition and device preferences usage.# Review — Meet Call Functionality & Backend Requirements

## 1. Overview

The **meet-call feature is currently a frontend-complete, mock-first implementation.** The client already ships a Google‑Meet-style UI, a state store, a REST API module, routing, and socket event emissions. However, **every real path is disabled** (`_mockMode: true`) and **no backend exists yet**. The real integration is stubbed where the browser can't fake it (WebRTC transport, signalling, presence).

> **Key takeaway**
> To make meets actually work, the backend must implement **socket signalling events, meet session lifecycle, WebRTC signalling (offer/answer/ICE) or an SFU, ICE server distribution, and targeted invitations via user presence.**

---

## 2. What Exists Today (Frontend Inventory)

### 2.1 State store — `src/store/meets.js` (registered as `meets`)

| Area | Details |
| :--- | :--- |
| **State** | `activeMeets`, `incomingInvitations`, `meetHistory`, `currentMeetId`, `meetStatus` (`idle/ringing/connecting/active/ending`), `availableDevices`, `isMuted`, `isAudioTestActive`, `_mockMode: true`, `_mockDurationTimers`, `_mockStreams` |
| **Getters** | `currentMeet`, `allActiveMeets`, `isInMeet`, `recentMeetHistory`, `incomingInvitationCount`, `meetForId`, `deviceCount` |
| **Actions (browser-only)** | `enumerateDevices`, `requestMicrophone`, `testAudioOutput` |
| **Actions (lifecycle)** | `initiateMeet`, `joinMeet`, `leaveMeet`, `endMeet`, `toggleMute`, `acceptInvitation`, `rejectInvitation`, `handleIncomingInvitation` |
| **Mock helpers** | `setMockMode`, `_startMockDurationTimer`, `_stopMockDurationTimer`, `mockIncomingInvitation`, `clearMeets` |

In non-mock mode the store emits socket events through `$storex.session.emit(...)`:

```js
// src/store/meets.js  (non-mock branches)
session.emit({ event: 'meet-initiate',    data: { meetId, from, fromName, fromAvatar, participants, timestamp } })
session.emit({ event: 'meet-join',        data: { meetId, userId, timestamp } })
session.emit({ event: 'meet-leave',       data: { meetId, userId, timestamp } })
session.emit({ event: 'meet-end',         data: { meetId, endedBy, timestamp } })
session.emit({ event: 'meet-mute-toggle', data: { meetId, muted, userId, timestamp } })
session.emit({ event: 'meet-accept',      data: { meetId, acceptedBy, timestamp } })
session.emit({ event: 'meet-reject',      data: { meetId, rejectedBy, timestamp } })
```

### 2.2 REST API module — `src/api/modules/meets.js` (`API.meets`)

Documented endpoints (currently **never invoked** by the store — dead code / future use):

| Method | HTTP | Endpoint |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `initiateMeet` | POST | `/api/meets/initiate` |
| `joinMeet` | POST | `/api/meets/join` |
| `leaveMeet` | POST | `/api/meets/leave` |
| `endMeet` | POST | `/api/meets/end` |
| `listActiveMeets` | GET | `/api/meets` |
| `getMeetInfo` | GET | `/api/meets/:meetId` |
| `sendOffer` | POST | `/api/meets/:meetId/signal/offer` |
| `sendAnswer` | POST | `/api/meets/:meetId/signal/answer` |
| `addIceCandidate` | POST | `/api/meets/:meetId/signal/ice-candidate` |
| `getDevices` / `requestMicrophone` / `requestCamera` / `requestMedia` / `testAudioOutput` | — | **Browser-only, no backend needed** |

### 2.3 Views & components

| File | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- |
| `src/views/MeetView.vue` | Pre-join lobby, active-call grid, local camera, **multi** screen-share, participants, side chat panel, settings, invite. Uses `getUserMedia` / `getDisplayMedia`, reads `$route.params.meetId`. |
| `src/components/meet/MeetHeader.vue` | Title, meet id, live/status badge |
| `src/components/meet/MeetControls.vue` | Mute / camera / screen-share / invite / settings / leave / end |
| `src/components/meet/MeetParticipants.vue` | Participant list + mute indicators |
| `src/components/meet/MeetInviteModal.vue` | Copy meet id, copy invite link, invite online users, emit `meet-invitation` |
| `src/components/meet/MeetSettingsPanel.vue` / `MeetSettingsModal.vue` | Device selection, mic/speaker test, volume, camera preview (persisted to `localStorage["meetSettings"]`) |

### 2.4 Routing, navigation & config

| Layer | Wiring |
| :--- | :--- |
| `src/router/index.ts` | `/:projectName/meet` (name `meet`), `/:projectName/meet/:meetId` (name `meet-session`) |
| `src/router/navigate.js` | `routes.meet`, `$navigation.meets.open(meetId)`, `getMeetId()`, `isMeetView`, `hasMeetContext` |
| `src/config/apps.js` | `APPS.meet` (id/title/component + route + desktopParams `{ meetId }`) |
| `src/config/appComponentsMap.js` | `'meet': MeetView` |
| `src/store/ui.js` | `openMeet(meetId)` → `openApp({ appKey: 'meet', ... })`; plus `callDevicePreferences`, `setCallDevicePreferences`, `activeChatCallPanelWidth` |

### 2.5 Socket event handling — `src/store/session.js`

`onEvent` currently reacts to **`voice-call-*`** events and dispatches to **`$storex.calls.*`**:

```js
// src/store/session.js
if (event === 'voice-call-initiate')  $storex.calls.handleIncomingCall(...)
if (event === 'voice-call-accept')    $storex.calls.updateCallStatus(...)
if (event === 'voice-call-reject')    $storex.calls.endActiveCall(...)
if (event === 'voice-call-end')       $storex.calls.endActiveCall(...)
if (event === 'voice-call-participant-added') $storex.calls.addParticipantToCall(...)
if (event === 'voice-call-mute-toggle') { /* log only */ }
```

> ⚠️ **This is a mismatch / latent bug.** There is **no `calls` store** (modules are `... meets ...`), and the meets store emits **`meet-*`** event names. So server replies in the `voice-call-*` shape would throw (`$storex.calls` is `undefined`), and replies in the `meet-*` shape are currently **not handled at all** for incoming events.

---

## 3. How a Meet "Works" Today (Mock Flow)

```text
User → "Start call" → meets.initiateMeet()
        └─ addActiveMeet + setCurrentMeet + status 'connecting'
        └─ after ~1200 ms → status 'active' + mock duration timer
        └─ (mockMode) NO network activity

User → "Invite" → MeetInviteModal → (mockMode) local toast only
        └─ (real) session.emit('meet-invitation', { meetId, to, from, inviteLink })

Remote participants → rendered as static placeholder tiles (no media)
```

Real media (camera/mic/screen) is **only local preview** — there is **no `RTCPeerConnection` anywhere in the client**, so remote audio/video is not actually transported yet.

---

## 4. Backend Requirements

### 4.1 Socket.IO signalling events (required)

**Client → Server** (already emitted by the store / invite modal):

| Event | Payload | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `meet-initiate` | `{ meetId, from, fromName, fromAvatar, participants[], timestamp }` | Start a session, ring/notify participants |
| `meet-invitation` | `{ meetId, to, from, inviteLink, timestamp }` | Target a specific user invite |
| `meet-join` | `{ meetId, userId, timestamp }` | Join room |
| `meet-accept` | `{ meetId, acceptedBy, timestamp }` | Accept invite |
| `meet-reject` | `{ meetId, rejectedBy, timestamp }` | Reject invite |
| `meet-leave` | `{ meetId, userId, timestamp }` | Leave (session continues) |
| `meet-end` | `{ meetId, endedBy, timestamp }` | End for everyone |
| `meet-mute-toggle` | `{ meetId, muted, userId, timestamp }` | Broadcast mute state |

**Server → Client** (must be delivered, ideally targeted per user):

| Event | Payload | Should drive (store action) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `meet-invitation` / `meet-initiate` | `{ meetId, from, fromName, fromAvatar, timestamp }` | `meets.handleIncomingInvitation(...)` |
| `meet-join` / `meet-participant-added` | `{ meetId, userId }` | `meets.addParticipantToMeet(...)` |
| `meet-accept` | `{ meetId, acceptedBy }` | `meets.updateMeetStatus({ status:'active' })` |
| `meet-reject` / `meet-leave` | `{ meetId, userId }` | remove participant / close |
| `meet-end` | `{ meetId, endedBy }` | `meets.endActiveMeet(meetId)` |
| `meet-mute-toggle` | `{ meetId, userId, muted }` | update participant mute UI |
| **WebRTC signal** (e.g. `meet-signal`) | `{ meetId, from, to, offer/answer/candidate }` | peer connection handshake |

### 4.2 REST endpoints (if the REST strategy is preferred over sockets)

Implement as documented in `api/modules/meets.js`:

```text
POST /api/meets/initiate
POST /api/meets/join
POST /api/meets/leave
POST /api/meets/end
GET  /api/meets
GET  /api/meets/:meetId
POST /api/meets/:meetId/signal/offer
POST /api/meets/:meetId/signal/answer
POST /api/meets/:meetId/signal/ice-candidate
```

> Note: the store's real path uses **sockets**, not these REST calls. Pick one signalling transport and keep the client + these route names consistent (either wire the store to `API.meets.*` or route signalling through sockets). Right now the two strategies are disconnected.

### 4.3 WebRTC infrastructure (required for real media)

- **Signalling transport** — room-scoped relay of SDP offer/answer and ICE candidates (socket events or the `/signal/*` endpoints).
- **ICE servers endpoint** — the client needs STUN/TURN config (e.g. `GET /api/meets/ice-servers` or included in `initiate`/`join` responses). Required for NAT traversal; TURN credentials ideally short-lived.
- **Topology decision:**
  - *Mesh* (P2P, `RTCPeerConnection` per pair) — fine for small calls; needs N-1 connections.
  - *SFU/MCU* (e.g. LiveKit, mediasoup, Janus, Jitsi, coturn for TURN) — needed for larger calls, server-side mixing/forwarding, and recording.
- **Server-side room registry** — track participants per `meetId`, allowed to enforce who can join/end.

### 4.4 Presence & targeted delivery (required)

`MeetInviteModal` builds its invite list from `$storex.users.onlineUsers`, which is populated by the existing **`codx-junior-online-users`** socket event. The backend must:

- Broadcast online users (already implemented for chat).
- Support **per-user rooms** (e.g. `user:<username>` / socket id) so `meet-invitation` can be delivered to a specific `to`.
- Map username ↔ socket(s), with multi-tab/device support.

### 4.5 Session lifecycle, auth & permissions

- **Room model:** `meetId` → { initiator, participants[], status, started_at, ended_at, chat_id }.
- **Only initiator** can `end` (client UI gates "End Call" behind `isInitiator`; backend must enforce).
- **Authorization:** only invited/online authenticated users may `join`; reuse existing socket auth (`codx-junior-login`).
- **Server is source of truth** for participant list, mute states, and duration (so all clients agree).

### 4.6 Chat association (integration)

`MeetView` creates a meet chat via `$storex.chats.createNewChat({ name, temp:false })` (backed by `/api/chats`) and stores `chatId` on the local meet. Backend should:

- Persist the **`chat_id` ↔ meet** link so all participants open the same meet chat.
- Optionally expose meet messages/notes through the chat/analytics pipeline.

### 4.7 Persistence & history (optional / recommended)

`meetHistory` is currently in-memory only. If history should survive reloads, the backend needs:

```text
GET /api/meets/history          → past meets (participants, start/end, duration)
GET /api/meets/:meetId          → single meet record
```

---

## 5. Integration Gaps to Resolve (client + backend contract)

| # | Issue | Impact | Fix |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | `_mockMode: true` by default | No real signalling ever runs | Flip to `false` when backend is live (or gate via global setting) |
| 2 | `session.js` listens to `voice-call-*` and calls non-existent `$storex.calls` | Incoming meet events crash / are unhandled | Align backend + session handler on `meet-*` events, dispatch to `$storex.meets.*` |
| 3 | Store emits sockets but `API.meets.*` REST exists unused | Duplicate/divergent strategies | Choose one transport; delete or wire the other |
| 4 | No `RTCPeerConnection` in client | Remote audio/video not transported | Add peer-connection layer + backend signalling/ICE |
| 5 | Invite link = `${origin}/meet/${meetId}` (no `projectName`) | Link 404s (routes need `/:projectName/meet/:meetId`) | Include project segment: `${origin}/${projectName}/meet/${meetId}` |
| 6 | Duration timer is mock-only | Real duration not tracked | Server-side `started_at`/duration, broadcast to clients |

```text
Naming contract (recommended single source of truth)
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
incoming invite   → meet-invitation   { meetId, from, fromName, fromAvatar, timestamp }
participant join  → meet-join         { meetId, userId }
accept / reject   → meet-accept / meet-reject
end / leave       → meet-end / meet-leave
mute              → meet-mute-toggle  { meetId, userId, muted }
webrtc            → meet-signal       { meetId, from, to, offer|answer|candidate }
```

---

## 6. Suggested Backend Data Model

```jsonc
// MeetSession
{
  "meet_id": "meet_1720000000_ab12cd",
  "name": "Meet 14:05",
  "initiator": "alice",
  "participants": ["alice", "bob"],
  "status": "active",              // connecting | active | ended
  "chat_id": "uuid-or-null",
  "started_at": 1720000000000,
  "ended_at": null,
  "duration": 0,
  "mutes": { "alice": false, "bob": true },
  "project_id": "codx-junior"
}
```

```jsonc
// ICE config response
{ "iceServers": [ { "urls": "stun:stun.host:3478" },
                  { "urls": "turn:turn.host:3478", "username": "…", "credential": "…" } ] }
```

---

## 7. Backend Delivery Checklist

| Layer | Item | Status (needed) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Socket | `meet-*` lifecycle events (client→server) | ☐ |
| Socket | `meet-*` broadcast events (server→client) | ☐ |
| Socket | Per-user targeting rooms for invitations | ☐ |
| Socket/REST | WebRTC signalling (offer/answer/ICE) relay | ☐ |
| REST | `/api/meets/initiate\|join\|leave\|end` | ☐ |
| REST | `/api/meets` and `/api/meets/:meetId` | ☐ |
| REST | ICE servers endpoint | ☐ |
| Infra | STUN/TURN (coturn) and/or SFU | ☐ |
| Auth | Room join authorization + initiator-only end | ☐ |
| Model | MeetSession persistence + chat link | ☐ |
| Model | Meet history endpoint (optional) | ☐ |
| Client | Flip `_mockMode` off + fix `session.js` event names | ☐ (client) |
| Client | Add `RTCPeerConnection` media transport | ☐ (client) |

---

## 8. File Reference Map

| File | Role in meet feature |
| :--- | :--- |
| `src/store/meets.js` | Meet state machine, socket emits, mock engine |
| `src/api/modules/meets.js` | REST endpoint definitions (currently unused) |
| `src/views/MeetView.vue` | Main meet screen (lobby, call, chat, panel) |
| `src/components/meet/*.vue` | Header, controls, participants, invite, settings |
| `src/store/session.js` | Socket event router (**mismatched `voice-call-*` / `$storex.calls`**) |
| `src/store/ui.js` | `openMeet`, call device preferences |
| `src/config/apps.js`, `src/config/appComponentsMap.js` | App registration + component map |
| `src/router/index.ts`, `src/router/navigate.js` | `meet` / `meet-session` routes & openers |

---

## 9. Summary

- ✅ **Frontend feature is fully scaffolded** (UI, store, routes, config, invite flow) and works end-to-end in **mock mode**.
- ⚠️ **Real functionality is inert**: mock gated, no WebRTC peer transport, and a **session/event naming mismatch** (`voice-call-*` vs `meet-*`, `$storex.calls` vs `$storex.meets`).
- 🔧 **Backend must provide**: `meet-*` socket lifecycle events, targeted invitations via user rooms, WebRTC signalling relay (or SFU), ICE/STUN/TURN config, meet session lifecycle + auth, and (recommended) an optional `chat_id` link and meet history.

Would you like me to (a) draft the exact **backend event/route contract as an OpenAPI/socket spec**, or (b) prepare the **client-side fixes** (flip `_mockMode`, correct `session.js` handlers, fix the invite URL, add the `RTCPeerConnection` layer)? I can also drop this review into a persistent doc (e.g. `docs/meet-calls.md`) if you want it versioned.

# Meets API — Client Integration Guide

How the codx-junior client connects to and uses the **meets** (WebRTC call) API.

This guide documents the contract implemented by the backend router `codx/junior/api/meets.py`
together with the `meetsModule` in `client/src/api/modules/meets.js`.

---

## 1. Overview

A **meet** is a single call session. Participants join a meet and exchange WebRTC
signalling data (SDP offer/answer and ICE candidates) so their browsers can open a
peer-to-peer connection.

The client interacts with the backend over **two channels**:

| Channel | Used for | Where |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **REST (HTTP)** | Lifecycle + signalling submission | `/api/meets/...` |
| **Socket.IO** | Real-time delivery of lifecycle + signalling events | path `/api/socket.io` |

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    C[Client] -->|REST: initiate/join/leave/end| R[Meets router]
    C -->|REST: offer/answer/ice-candidate| R
    R --> M[(MeetManager)]
    R -->|emit| S[Socket.IO server]
    S -->|codx-junior-meet| C
    S -->|codx-junior-meet-signal| C
```

> **Key idea:** the REST call *records* the action and the Socket.IO event *delivers* it
> to the other participants. A client that only uses REST will never receive remote
> signals — it must also listen on Socket.IO.

---

## 2. Connection Basics

### 2.1 Base URL

All REST endpoints live under the `/api` prefix (the router declares `prefix="/meets"`):

```
<host>/api/meets/<...>
```

The browser client already calls them through the shared `API` helper, for example:

```js /client/src/api/modules/meets.js
const result = await API.post('/api/meets/initiate', { meetId, name, participants, timestamp })
```

### 2.2 Authentication & identity

The backend resolves the **caller identity** from the request headers
(see `_resolve_identity` in `meets.py`):

| Header | Meaning | Required |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `authentication` | `Bearer <token>` (or any scheme; the last segment after a space is used) | No — falls back to `x-username` |
| `x-username` | Username when there is no authenticated user | No — falls back to `"guest"` |
| `x-sid` | Socket.IO session id used to target signalling (`fromSid` in events) | Recommended for signalling |

> **Note:** meets endpoints do **not** reject unauthenticated requests.
> If no user is present, the participant is registered as `guest`.
> Always send `x-sid` alongside `authentication` so remote peers can reply to the right session.

### 2.3 Socket.IO channel

The Socket.IO server is mounted at path **`/api/socket.io`** and broadcasts with CORS
`*`. Reuse the application's existing Socket.IO connection where possible.

```js
import { io } from 'socket.io-client'

const socket = io(window.location.origin, {
  path: '/api/socket.io',
  transports: ['websocket', 'polling'],
})

// Register the session so the backend can map sid -> user
socket.emit('codx-junior-login', {
  user: {
    token: /* current auth token */,
    username: /* current username */,
    avatar: /* current avatar url */,
  },
})
```

> The snippet above is illustrative — adapt it to the socket client already used by the app.
> The relevant facts are: **path** `/api/socket.io` and the **login event** `codx-junior-login`.

---

## 3. Getting Started — End-to-End Flow

### Steps at a glance

1. Connect Socket.IO and register listeners (lifecycle + signal events).
2. Acquire media (optional, browser-only).
3. **Initiator:** `POST /api/meets/initiate`, then create an SDP offer and send it.
4. **Joiner:** `POST /api/meets/join`, receive the offer, then send an SDP answer.
5. Both exchange ICE candidates as they are discovered.
6. On exit: `POST /api/meets/leave` (participant) or `POST /api/meets/end` (initiator).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Initiator
    participant API as Meets router
    participant SIO as Socket.IO
    participant B as Joiner

    A->>API: POST /api/meets/initiate
    API-->>SIO: codx-junior-meet (initiated)
    SIO-->>B: codx-junior-meet (initiated)
    B->>API: POST /api/meets/join
    A->>API: POST /.../signal/offer
    API-->>SIO: codx-junior-meet-signal (offer)
    SIO-->>B: codx-junior-meet-signal (offer)
    B->>API: POST /.../signal/answer
    API-->>SIO: codx-junior-meet-signal (answer)
    SIO-->>A: codx-junior-meet-signal (answer)
    A->>API: POST /.../signal/ice-candidate
    B->>API: POST /.../signal/ice-candidate
    A->>API: POST /api/meets/leave
    B->>API: POST /api/meets/end
```

---

## 4. REST Endpoints Reference

### 4.1 Lifecycle

| Method & Path | Purpose | Body |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `POST /api/meets/initiate` | Create (or reactivate) a meet, register the initiator | `{ meetId?, name?, participants?, timestamp? }` |
| `POST /api/meets/join` | Add the caller as a participant | `{ meetId, timestamp? }` |
| `POST /api/meets/leave` | Remove the caller from a meet | `{ meetId, timestamp? }` |
| `POST /api/meets/end` | End the meet (typically the initiator) | `{ meetId, timestamp? }` |

**Responses** (all lifecycle endpoints):

```jsonc
// initiate / join / leave / end
{ "success": true, "meet": { /* Meet object, see §7 */ } }
```

**Examples**

```js
// Initiate
const { meet } = await API.post('/api/meets/initiate', {
  meetId: 'demo-room',
  name: 'Daily standup',
  participants: ['alice', 'bob'],
  timestamp: Date.now(),
})

// Join
await API.post('/api/meets/join', { meetId: 'demo-room', timestamp: Date.now() })

// Leave
await API.post('/api/meets/leave', { meetId: 'demo-room', timestamp: Date.now() })

// End (initiator only)
await API.post('/api/meets/end', { meetId: 'demo-room', timestamp: Date.now() })
```

> `meetId` is optional on **initiate** (a UUID is generated when omitted) but is
> **required** on `join`, `leave`, and `end` — a missing `meetId` returns `400`.

These are also available as module methods: `initiateMeet`, `joinMeet`, `leaveMeet`, `endMeet`.

### 4.2 Query

| Method & Path | Purpose | Response |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `GET /api/meets` | List meets (active only by default) | `{ success, count, meets: [Meet, ...] }` |
| `GET /api/meets/{meetId}` | Get one meet's details/status | `{ success, meet }` |

```js
const active = await API.get('/api/meets')          // listActiveMeets()
const info   = await API.get(`/api/meets/${meetId}`) // getMeetInfo()
```

> `GET /api/meets` also accepts the query flag `?active=false` to include ended meets.

### 4.3 WebRTC signalling

| Method & Path | Purpose | Body |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `POST /api/meets/{meetId}/signal/offer` | Relay an SDP offer | `{ offer, to?, timestamp? }` |
| `POST /api/meets/{meetId}/signal/answer` | Relay an SDP answer | `{ answer, to?, timestamp? }` |
| `POST /api/meets/{meetId}/signal/ice-candidate` | Relay an ICE candidate | `{ candidate, to?, timestamp? }` |

**Response:**

```jsonc
{ "success": true, "meetId": "demo-room", "type": "offer", "to": "bob" }
```

**Examples**

```js
// Send an SDP offer to a specific peer (or omit `to` to broadcast)
await API.post(`/api/meets/${meetId}/signal/offer`, { offer, to: 'bob', timestamp: Date.now() })

// Answer an offer
await API.post(`/api/meets/${meetId}/signal/answer`, { answer, to: 'alice', timestamp: Date.now() })

// Trickle an ICE candidate
await API.post(`/api/meets/${meetId}/signal/ice-candidate`, { candidate, to: 'bob', timestamp: Date.now() })
```

Module methods: `sendOffer`, `sendAnswer`, `addIceCandidate`.

> Posting a signal for an unknown `meetId` returns `404`.
> `to` is a target **username or sid**; an empty `to` means "broadcast to the meet".

---

## 5. Socket.IO Events Reference

Register these listeners once, right after connecting.

### 5.1 `codx-junior-meet` — lifecycle events

Payload:

```jsonc
{
  "type": "initiated" | "joined" | "left" | "ended",
  "meetId": "demo-room",
  "from": "alice",
  "meet": { /* present on "initiated" */ },
  "participants": ["alice", "bob"]   // present on "joined" / "left"
}
```

```js
socket.on('codx-junior-meet', (evt) => {
  switch (evt.type) {
    case 'initiated': /* a new meet exists */ break
    case 'joined':    /* update participant list from evt.participants */ break
    case 'left':      /* a participant left */ break
    case 'ended':     /* tear down the call UI */ break
  }
})
```

### 5.2 `codx-junior-meet-signal` — WebRTC signalling

Payload:

```jsonc
{
  "meetId": "demo-room",
  "type": "offer" | "answer" | "ice-candidate",
  "from": "alice",           // sender username
  "fromSid": "abc123",       // sender Socket.IO session id
  "to": "bob",               // target ("" = broadcast)
  "signal": { /* raw SDP or ICE candidate payload */ }
}
```

```js
socket.on('codx-junior-meet-signal', async (evt) => {
  // Ignore anything not addressed to us
  if (evt.to && evt.to !== myUsername && evt.to !== mySid) return

  switch (evt.type) {
    case 'offer':
      await pc.setRemoteDescription(new RTCSessionDescription(evt.signal))
      const answer = await pc.createAnswer()
      await pc.setLocalDescription(answer)
      await API.post(`/api/meets/${evt.meetId}/signal/answer`, {
        answer, to: evt.from, timestamp: Date.now(),
      })
      break
    case 'answer':
      await pc.setRemoteDescription(new RTCSessionDescription(evt.signal))
      break
    case 'ice-candidate':
      if (evt.signal) await pc.addIceCandidate(new RTCIceCandidate(evt.signal))
      break
  }
})
```

> The candidate you POST is echoed back verbatim inside `signal`; feed it straight into
> `RTCPeerConnection.addIceCandidate`.

---

## 6. Error Handling

REST endpoints signal failures with standard FastAPI errors:

| Status | Cause | Client action |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `400` | `meetId` missing, or the meet is not active (join) | Prompt to create/choose a meet |
| `404` | Unknown `meetId` | Remove the stale meet from UI |
| `422` | Body failed validation | Check the payload shape |

Socket.IO emission is **best-effort**: if the server cannot broadcast, the HTTP call
still succeeds. Do not rely on the event as the sole confirmation of an action —
treat the REST response as the source of truth and the event as a convenience.

---

## 7. Data Models

### 7.1 Meet

| Field | Type | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `meet_id` | string | Unique id (generated if omitted on initiate) |
| `name` | string | Human readable name |
| `initiator` | string | Username that created the meet |
| `status` | `"active"` \| `"ended"` | Lifecycle status |
| `participants` | `MeetParticipant[]` | Currently connected |
| `invited` | string[] | Invited usernames |
| `signals` | `MeetSignal[]` | Server-side signalling history (capped) |
| `project_id` | string \| null | Owning project, when a session is present |
| `created_at` / `updated_at` / `ended_at` | ISO-8601 string | Timestamps |

### 7.2 MeetParticipant

| Field | Type |
| :--- | :--- |
| `sid` | string \| null |
| `username` | string |
| `name` | string |
| `avatar` | string |
| `is_initiator` | boolean |
| `audio` / `video` / `screen` / `muted` | boolean |
| `joined_at` / `updated_at` | ISO-8601 string |

### 7.3 MeetSignal

| Field | Type | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `type` | `"offer"` \| `"answer"` \| `"ice-candidate"` | |
| `sender` | string | Username or sid |
| `to` | string | Target (empty = broadcast) |

/**
 * Extracts code blocks with file paths from markdown content
 * Pattern: ```lang /path/to/file
 */
export function extractCodeBlocks(content) {
  if (!content || typeof content !== 'string') return []

  const codeBlocks = []
  const lines = content.split('\n')
  let i = 0

  while (i < lines.length) {
    const line = lines[i]
    const match = line.match(/^```(\w+)\s+(.+)$/)

    if (match) {
      const language = match[1]
      const filePath = match[2].trim()

      // Only include blocks with file paths
      if (filePath) {
        const blockContent = []
        i++

        // Collect lines until closing ```
        while (i < lines.length && lines[i] !== '```') {
          blockContent.push(lines[i])
          i++
        }

        codeBlocks.push({
          language,
          filePath,
          content: blockContent.join('\n'),
          fileName: filePath.split('/').pop()
        })
      }
    }
    i++
  }

  return codeBlocks
}

/**
 * Checks if content has extractable code blocks with file paths
 */
export function hasCodeBlocksWithPaths(content) {
  return extractCodeBlocks(content).length > 0
}
